IS IT A NAVIGATION REFERENCE? YES, and that is the authority's own framing: the companion value TuGLW is longnamed 'verkehrsgesicherte Fahrrinnentiefe unter GlW (Tiefe unter GlW)' = the TRAFFIC-SECURED FAIRWAY DEPTH BENEATH GlW (Kaub 190 cm, Duisburg 280 cm) -- i.e. WSV defines the maintained navigable channel depth AS A DEPTH MEASURED DOWN FROM GlW. ⚠️ LABEL CORRECTION: TuGLW is a DEPTH, not a stage, and it currently sits in this folder's tables in a row of stage values where it reads as one. DEFINITION AND DERIVATION (from WSV/BfG documentation, NOT from the API which gives only the gloss 'Pegelkennwert: GLW gleichwertiger Wasserstand'): GlW is the stage equalled or undercut on average 20 ice-free days per year, derived by first computing the equivalent discharge GlQ from ~100 years of daily mean discharge at the gauge, then converting GlQ to a stage via measured water-surface elevations at discharges near GlQ. It is the reference the WSV uses to set planned fairway depth per Rhine reach. ⇒ GlW is a DURATION-CURVE NAVIGATION REFERENCE, categorically different from NNW. 🔴 AND NNW IS NOW PINNED AT THE PRIMARY TOO: PEGELONLINE's own definitions page gives 'Pegelkennwert: NNW niedrigster bekannter TAGESMITTELWERT des Wasserstandes' = lowest known DAILY MEAN stage. detail: 🔴 COMMISSIONED (AEOLUS follow-up #2) AND ESTABLISHED FROM THE DOCUMENTS -- the apparent contradiction is not a contradiction. Source: 2027-2028OperatingGuidelines_Final.pdf (usbr.gov/ColoradoRiverBasin/post2026/decision-doc/, HTTP 200, 1,008,363 B, 48,731 chars via pdfminer). §5.1.C.2 VERBATIM: 'If the Exhibit Run of the August 24-Month Study assuming a release of 7.0 maf (from Section 5.1.C.1) results in Lake Powell elevation projected to decline below 3,510 feet AT ANY TIME DURING THE WATER YEAR, defer the determination of the Water Year release until April and proceed as follows in Table 1 below.' Table 1's own heading repeats it: 'when Lake Powell elevation is less than 3,510 feet in the August 24-Month Study Exhibit Run'. ⇒ THE TEST HAS FOUR PARTS, ALL NOW ESTABLISHED: (1) VINTAGE = the AUGUST study, not the current month -- which is why the September study RE-STATES the August determination rather than re-deriving it; (2) RUN = an EXHIBIT RUN, defined in the Guidelines' own definitions section as 'modeling performed IN ADDITION TO the official modeling runs... Exhibit Runs reflect unofficial dam operations or sensitivity analysis based on hypothetical conditions or dam operations' -- i.e. NOT among the published files; (3) ASSUMED RELEASE = 7.0 maf; (4) BASIS = 'at any time during the Water Year', a WITHIN-WINDOW MINIMUM, not a year-end or month-end endpoint. INFLOW SCENARIO IS ALSO SETTLED: the Guidelines define 'Most Probable' as 'a modeling projection provided by Reclamation in the monthly 24-Month Study, which simulates conditions using a median (50th percentile exceedance) inflow scenario' -- so the test keys to the MOST PROBABLE run, NOT the Probable Minimum. ⇒ WHY THE PUBLISHED TABLES CANNOT FALSIFY THE CLAIM: Table 1's Aug row requires 'at least 2 official August 24-Month Studies... Runs assume a Water Year release of 6.0 maf and 7.0 maf. ALL RUNS INCLUDE THE SAME RELEASE PATTERN Oct-Apr THAT MAINTAINS A MINIMUM TARGET ELEVATION OF 3,510 FEET in March of the following year.' The two published Most Probable files ARE those two official runs, and they are CONSTRUCTED to hold 3,510. They never dip below it BY DESIGN -- that is the consequence of the trigger having fired, not evidence against it. CORROBORATION IN THE NUMBERS: the 7 maf run prints EXACTLY 3,510.00 at Feb-2028 in BOTH the August and September studies (and 3,510.10 / 3,510.00 at Mar-2028) -- a modelled floor pinned to the target, not a coincidence. ⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE C6 GATE: a leg worded 'Powell below 3,510 ft' CANNOT BE GRADED FROM ANY PUBLISHED 24-MS TABLE. The operative instrument is an Exhibit Run that Reclamation does not publish; what IS observable is the DETERMINATION (deferral to April, the 6.0-7.0 maf range statement, Table 1 being in force) and the ACTUAL daily elevation. Also recorded, the next leg down: §5.1.D keys on 'Based on ANY 24-Month Study, if Lake Powell is projected to decline below 3,500 feet at any time from the current month through March of the following year' -- a WIDER run basis ('any') and a different window than §5.1.C.

detail: STANDING RULE, AEOLUS-ruled 2026-09-18 (KB-148), recorded here because this is the file a future water worker reads. RULE: run `date` immediately before writing ANY pulled_at, and ANY stamp later than the wall clock STOPS THE WRITE. It is a blocking defect on this desk, not a cosmetic one. WHY -- AEOLUS's framing is sharper than my own disclosure was and is the part worth keeping: pulled_at is the column a staleness check reads, AND THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR DECIDES WHETHER IT IS SURVIVABLE. A stamp in the PAST makes a row look STALER than it is -> the nudge fires, someone looks -> FAILS LOUD. A stamp in the FUTURE makes a row look FRESHER than it is -> the check is satisfied, nobody looks, the row is trusted past its real half-life -> FAILS SILENT. ⚠️ AND THE ASYMMETRY IS NOT RANDOM: a narrative-derived stamp DRIFTS FORWARD under load (session clocks run ahead of the wall clock as a session lengthens), so this error class SYSTEMATICALLY produces the silent direction. My own instance: 71 rows stamped '15:2x ET' when the clock read 14:10 -- an hour ahead, in the silent direction, in already-delivered output, in a column nobody was going to audit. I caught it only because I re-read the clock for an unrelated reason. NOTE FOR AEOLUS: this may deserve a line in water/AGENT.md's hard limits, which is AEOLUS's file to change, not mine.
